summary: Edward Denison Ross worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies, Tibetology, and history and archaeology. Educated at University College London (~1887–1891), he held posts there (~1896–1901), at the British Museum (1914), and served as head of SOAS (~1916–1937).

Edward Elbridge Salisbury worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Yale and in Europe under Woolsey, Burnouf, de Sacy, Garcin de Tassy, Bopp, and Lassen. He was Professor of Arabic and Sanskrit at Yale (1841–1854).
Edward Espe Brown is a scholar in Buddhist studies. He studied under traditional teachers Shunryu Suzuki (~1966–1971), Reb Anderson, and Jack Kornfield.

Edward Fitzpatrick Crangle specializes in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He completed his doctoral studies under Roderick S. Bucknell (attested 1994) and held a post at the University of Sydney.

Edward Garrett works in linguistics and Tibetology. He earned his PhD at UCLA (~1996–2001) under Carson Schütze and Dominique Sportiche, and undertook postdoctoral study under Anna Szabolcsi. He held research assistant posts at UCLA (1996–2000) and the University of Virginia (2000–2001).

Edward Granville Browne specialized in Iranian and Central Asian studies and linguistics. After studying at Pembroke College, Cambridge (~1879–1882), he served as Adams Professor of Arabic at the University of Cambridge from ~1902 to 1926.
Edward H. Schafer was a sinologist who studied at UCLA (~1931–1934), UC Berkeley (~1937–1947), and Harvard (~1940–1941). He served as a professor at UC Berkeley from ~1947 to 1984.

Edward James Rapson worked in Indology, linguistics, and history and archaeology. Educated at St John's College, Cambridge (~1879–1883), he worked at the British Museum (~1887–1906) and UCL (~1903–1906) before serving as professor of Sanskrit at Cambridge (~1906–1936).

Edward Joseph Thomas worked in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at the University of St Andrews, held a post at Cambridge University Library (~1909–1939), and was attested as a professor at the University of Cambridge in 1946.

Edward Washburn Hopkins was an Indology, linguistics, and religious studies scholar. He studied at Columbia and Leipzig under Ernst Windisch and Albrecht Weber. He held professorships at Bryn Mawr College (1885–1895) and Yale University (1895–1926).

Edward Winslow Bastian works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Banaras Hindu University and the University of Wisconsin-Madison (PhD -1980 under Geshe Lhundub Sopa), also studying under Geshe Lobsang Tenzin, Geshe Lobsang, and Geshe Lobsang Donyo.
Edwin Arnold worked in Indology and Buddhist studies. His education included studies at King's School, Rochester, King's College London (~1847–1850), and University College, Oxford (~1850–1854).

Edwin F. Bryant specializes in Indology, religious studies, and philosophy. He studied at Columbia University (~1990–1997) and held academic posts at Harvard University (~1999–2003) and Rutgers University (~2003).

Edwin Felix Thomas Atkinson was an Indology and history/archaeology scholar who studied at Trinity College Dublin (~1857–1861). He served as President of the Asiatic Society (~1886–1888) and Accountant General for the Government of Bengal (~1888–1890).

Edwin Gerow is a scholar in Indology and philosophy. He served as Professor of Religion and Humanities at Reed College (~1985–1999) and Editor-in-Chief of the Journal of the American Oriental Society (~1994–1998).

Edwin Whitfield Fay was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Rhodes College and Johns Hopkins under Bloomfield, Gildersleeve, Wright, Smyth, Warren, and Bright. He held posts at the University of Michigan (~1890–1891) and Washington and Lee University (~1893–1899).

Egaku Maeda was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1948–1957). He held posts at Meijo University and served as a professor at Aichi Gakuin University (~1969–1997).
Eiichi Yamaguchi works in the fields of Indology and philosophy. He was a graduate student at Kyushu University (attested 1986–1990) and later served as a research assistant there (attested 1991).

Eiki Hoshino specializes in religious studies and Buddhist studies. After studying at Taisho University (~1962–1970), he served there as a professor in the Faculty of Humanities and director (~1984–2014).

Eisaku Okada works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. After studying at Kyoto University (attested 2014), he held positions at the Japan Society for the Promotion of Science (2014), Koyasan University (2014), and Kyoto University (2015).
